test.name: Plan includes explicit fallback_for chain for church record search
test.description: The skill proposes a new plan for q_001 after prior census searches are exhausted. Church records are a logical next source, but Catholic parish records in Schuylkill County (Diocese, from 1875 Archdiocese, of Philadelphia until 1961) may not be digitized — so the plan must include a FamilySearch item as primary and a county-level diocesan archive as fallback_for it. Tests the Sequencing logic rubric dimension: fallback chains must appear in the plan when a primary source is likely to be unavailable.

input.delegation:
Create the next research plan for q_001. We've already done censuses — focus on what comes next, especially church and probate records.

judge_context: The plan must include at least one EXPLICIT fallback_for relationship: an item whose `fallback_for` field references another item's id. The plan for church or probate records in Schuylkill County should have a primary item (e.g., FamilySearch indexed collection) and a fallback item (e.g., diocesan archive or county courthouse) with `fallback_for` pointing to the primary. Whether that contingency structure reaches the persisted `fallback_for` field, rather than living only in rationale prose, is what Sequencing logic turns on for this test.
Free/indexed sources should precede paid/unindexed sources in sequence numbers. Probate on FamilySearch (free, partially indexed) should come before Ancestry (paid) fallback.

The rationale on the fallback item must explain WHY the primary might fail — e.g., 'Catholic parish registers may not yet be digitized; the parishes and the Archdiocese of Philadelphia archives hold the originals.'
